title: SSE fragmentation + resume protocol for robust streaming and structured tool outputs
creator: Ari Patel
description:
Problem summary: We need an SSE-based streaming contract that supports: (1) efficient, deterministic chunk/fragment framing for partial tokens and structured messages, (2) reconnection with resume semantics that avoid duplicate side-effects for function/tool calls, (3) compatibility with existing clients expecting simple 'data:' JSON lines as well as clients that parse function_call structured payloads, and (4) observability hooks for debugging partial outputs and latency regression detection.

Design proposal:
- Framing: adopt an explicit envelope JSON per SSE data line with fields {"frame_id","seq","type","payload","resume_hint"}. Each SSE "data: { ... }\n\n" line is a complete envelope. This keeps us compatible with naive SSE parsers and gives structured semantics for advanced clients.
  - frame_id: UUID for the logical response (stable across reconnects).
  - seq: increasing integer per event to detect gaps and reordering.
  - type: one of ["delta", "chunk", "function_call", "structured", "end", "resume_token"].
  - payload: string or nested JSON (serialized as a string to preserve single-line SSE).
  - resume_hint: optional compact token for quick resume (base62).

- Resume semantics: server emits explicit resume_token events with a cryptographic HMAC over (frame_id, last_seq, model_version, kv_cache_checkpoint_id). On client reconnect, clients send ?resume=token param. Server validates token and sends missing seqs or a short checkpoint summary to allow client to reconstruct. If the resume token is stale or KV checkpoint mismatch, server falls back to re-sending final full state (end) and annotates with "resume_failed" reason.

- Idempotency and tool/function calls: for messages of type "function_call" we include call_id and call_phase (start|stdout|end|error). call_id is globally unique per call in the frame_id namespace. On reconnect, clients should not re-issue local side-effects until they receive an "function_call:end" for that call_id. Server guarantees at-most-once delivery semantics for function_call:end by persisting minimal call metadata until acknowledged by the client (ack via ?ack=call_id on resume). This persistence is bounded and GC'd after 24 hours.

- Backpressure and partial tokens: we emit small "chunk" frames when tokenization boundaries are uncertain (for very low-latency mode). Clients interested in full tokens can buffer until a "delta" or "end" frames are received. We include estimated_remaining_tokens in some resume_hint payloads to guide clients.

- Compatibility layer: we will support two output modes selected by the client via ?mode=legacy|envelope. Legacy mode will emit plain SSE data lines containing the original flat JSON for backwards compatibility (data: {"text":"..."}). Envelope mode will use the new frame envelope. Both share the same frame_id and seq numbering so transitions during reconnect remain coherent.

- Observability: every envelope includes debug flags when sampling enabled: latency_ms, worker_id (masked), and kernel_profile_id. All resume_tokens and call_ids are logged to tracing with redaction for PII.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for framing encode/decode (including malformed lines).
- Integration tests for reconnect with resume_token success, token expiration, and KV checkpoint mismatch.
- End-to-end tests verifying no duplicate function_call:end semantics on reconnect.
- Backwards compatibility test validating legacy mode still parsable by existing SDKs.
- Load test to ensure increased metadata doesn't regress throughput >5% at 99th percentile.

Rollout plan: implement feature-gated support behind runtime flag and expose to internal canaries (10% traffic) for two weeks. Monitor duplicate function call rate, resume success rate, and increase canary to 50% then 100% if metrics stable.

Artifacts and links: GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/core/pull/1849 (draft), Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CORE/SSE+Envelope+and+Resume+Design, Perf dashboards: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/core/sse-framing
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ari Patel: Created initial proposal after incident where mobile SDKs saw duplicated function call side-effects during reconnects. Drafting envelope format to encode call_id and seq.

2025-02-13 - Maya Chen: Spike implemented encoder/decoder prototype; found edge case with Newline-in-payload requiring base64 fallback for structured payloads. Updated design to serialize payload as a single-line JSON string to preserve SSE assumptions.
2025-02-14 - Rahul Singh (code review): Concern about resume token size and exposure; recommended HMAC over condensed checkpoint id rather than full KV snapshot. Agreed — updated resume token design.
2025-02-16 - Design review (Elena Park): Verified compatibility mode acceptable; asked to include explicit SDK migration notes and example pseudocode for Node/Python. Added examples to design doc.
2025-02-18 - QA (Jordan Li): Started integration tests for reconnect scenarios; hitting intermittent failure when simulating partial GC of call metadata. Investigating persistence TTL and GC race.
test_plan: Automated unit tests for envelope encode/decode, integration tests for resume behavior, chaos tests simulating worker restarts and stale resume tokens, and SDK parser conformance tests (Node/Python/Go).
implementation_notes: Server will add small persisting store for call metadata keyed by (frame_id, call_id) with TTL=24h. Resume validation will check model_version and kv_checkpoint_id. We will add feature flag 'sse_envelope_v1' to gate rollout. Ensure telemetry emits resume_success, resume_failure_reason, duplicate_call_detected metrics.
release_notes_draft: Introduces an optional SSE envelope format with resume tokens and per-sequence framing. Backwards compatible legacy mode retained. Improves streaming resilience and prevents duplicate function/tool side-effects on reconnect. Release gated behind runtime flag. See Confluence for migration notes.
